dependencies.reason: uses its workspace record, its carry-patch settings, its access decision and its workspace lock
uses its repository store, its credential resolution and its capability report, which decides how a replaced patch tip is kept
applies every patch, detects every conflict and replays every recorded resolution through its history engine
turns the accepted patch-branch push of its receive path into a rebuild trigger
extends its sync route at the documented branch point for carry_patch workspaces

tasks.title: Add patches to the list, singly and in batches
steps: Add this task's behaviours to the patch routes' and patch list test files, and confirm they fail
Define the patch table with its position, status, origin fields and timestamps, with a migration the second target runs too

Implement the add: validate the branch name, the integration branch and the position, then resolve the branch locally, from the fork's fetched copy, or by fetching the fork under patch_branch_source origin, reporting which succeeded
Insert at the given position shifting the rest down, and append for a position past the end or an omitted one
Answer 200 with the existing patch for an if_not_exists hit and 409 without it

For a batch, check every element's syntax in array order before any branch lookup, then every branch before adding anything, refusing the whole batch on the first failure while leaving branches already created in place

Refuse a missing or empty branch name, the integration branch, a position below 1, a standard or archived workspace and an unresolvable branch with 400, prefixing a batch element's message with patch[i]
Refuse a duplicate branch and a branch repeated in a batch with 409, a held lock with 409 workspace_busy and a failed fork fetch with 502 origin_fetch_failed

tasks.title: Read and change patches, keeping the list contiguous
steps: Add this task's behaviours to the patch routes' test files, and confirm they fail
List a workspace's patches in position order without deleted ones, answering an empty array for a standard workspace
Read one patch, a deleted one included, reporting the SHA of a replaced tip where one is kept and omitting it where the lookup fails, without failing the request
Update only the position, status, description and upstream pull request a body names, ignoring any branch_name
Refuse an invalid status, the status deleted, an out-of-range position with 400, an unknown patch with 404 and a deleted patch with 409
Keep the positions contiguous from 1 after every operation, proved by a generative test over sequences of operations

tasks.title: Remove, restore and reorder patches
steps: Add this task's behaviours to the patch routes' test files, and confirm they fail
Remove a patch, close the positions, and discard any kept replaced tip on a best-effort basis that never changes the answer
Restore a deleted patch to the end of the list as active with its deleted time cleared
Reorder the whole list from a list of ids, setting positions in the order given
Refuse a reorder that is empty while patches exist, omits an id, repeats one or names a foreign patch with 400, and a restore of a patch that is not deleted with 400

tasks.title: Run the rebuild job
steps: Add this task's behaviours to the rebuild test files, and confirm they fail
Define the rebuild job record with its status, strategy, per-patch results and integration heads, and run it through the platform's queue
Take the workspace lock, fetch the upstream head, record it and release the lock before applying any patch
Apply the patches in position order through the history engine, skipping merged_upstream, disabled, deleted and branch-missing patches with their reasons
Replay a recorded resolution on a conflict, then end the job under fail_fast or mark the patch conflict and continue under continue
Write each patch's result as it finishes, so a reader of a running job sees the results so far
Retake the lock at the end, set the integration branch, mark merged_upstream patches deleted, close the positions and record the new and previous integration heads
Force-push the integration branch to the fork when rebuild_push_integration_branch is true, letting a failure leave the job completed
Detect a patch tip or upstream head that moved during the run, keep the result built from the tips the job started with and queue exactly one follow-up rebuild submitted by the system

tasks.title: Serve the rebuild routes
steps: Add this task's behaviours to the rebuild routes' test files, and confirm they fail
Implement the submit: check the workspace is carry_patch and ready, that a patch is active or conflict and that no rebuild is queued or running, then queue the job and answer 202
Take the strategy and fail mode from the body where given and from the workspace's settings otherwise
Refuse with 400 workspace_mode_mismatch, 400 no_active_patches, 400 for an unready workspace or an invalid field, and 409 concurrent_rebuild
Implement the list and the read, answering 404 for an unknown job and for one of another workspace
Implement cancel for a queued job and requeue for a dead-lettered one, answering 409 for any other status and for a requeue while another rebuild is queued or running
Implement rollback to a completed job's previous integration head, answering 409 for a job with no previous head, 409 workspace_busy for a held lock and 500 for a failed reset

Implement the preview: try every patch that is not disabled or merged upstream in position order against the upstream head and the patches before it that would succeed, report would_succeed with a tree or would_conflict with its files, report a missing branch as would_succeed, write nothing, and answer 400 for a standard workspace

tasks.title: Reset a patch branch to the fork
steps: Add this task's behaviours to the reset-to-origin test files, and confirm they fail
Check the preconditions in order: not archived and carry_patch, ready, the patch exists, not the integration branch, and the status is active, conflict or disabled
Fetch the branch from the fork and move it by the first rule that applies: created, none, fast_forwarded or replaced
Keep the old tip where this deployment keeps replaced tips when the move discards commits, superseding an earlier backup, and report it as replaced_sha
Record the patch as in sync at the fork's tip under patch_branch_source origin
Queue a rebuild when the branch moved and the patch is active or conflict, unless auto_rebuild_after_sync is false or one is already queued, and report whether one was queued and its id

Report missing_on_origin, ref_changed, workspace_busy, origin_fetch_failed and the read-back failure with their documented statuses, never leaving the patch record describing a move that did not happen

tasks.title: Extend the sync for a carry-patch workspace
steps: Add this task's behaviours to the carry-patch sync integration test file, and confirm they fail
Take over package 08's sync route at its documented branch point for carry_patch workspaces

Perform the steps in order: resolve the fork's credentials under patch_branch_source origin, fetch every upstream branch and the upstream head, fetch and prune the fork under origin, detect a force-push, refresh the patch branches, detect patches merged upstream, write the sync fields, queue a rebuild

Refresh each active, conflict or disabled patch's branch by the first rule that applies, under the divergence policy, never touching the integration branch, recording each patch's origin state, SHA and time and clearing all three under patch_branch_source hub

Detect patches merged upstream by ancestry, by content and by a pull request number in a recent upstream commit message, according to squash_merge_detection, clearing the origin fields of a matched patch
Queue one rebuild when the upstream advanced, an active or conflict patch's branch moved, or a patch became merged upstream, unless auto_rebuild_after_sync is false or one is already queued

On a branch refresh failure answer 500 with a message distinguishing the three cases, record the outcomes already reached, queue a rebuild for branches already moved, and write neither upstream_head_sha nor last_sync_at

Answer with the workspace plus patches_merged, rebuild_triggered, rebuild_job_id, force_push_detected, origin_fetched and, under patch_branch_source origin, patches_synced and patches_diverged, leaving sync_error unused and updating last_sync_at on every completed sync

tasks.title: Serve the rerere routes
steps: Add this task's behaviours to the rerere routes' test files, and confirm they fail
List a workspace's recorded resolutions newest first with their identity, path, recorded time and whether a resolution will be replayed, answering an empty array when there are none
Forget a resolution by identity, or by a path that is currently in conflict, answering 204 so the next occurrence is reported rather than replayed
Refuse an empty or invalid pathspec with 400 before the workspace is looked up, an unmatched identity or path with 404, and a held lock with 409 workspace_busy
Keep the slashes of a path pathspec while percent-encoding everything else, as the CLI reference requires

tasks.title: Serve the patch-status dashboard
steps: Add this task's behaviours to the dashboard test files, and confirm they fail
Assemble the workspace's state, its latest rebuild's id and status, every non-deleted patch in position order with its latest rebuild result, and the summary counts
Include a patch's conflicting files only where its latest rebuild result is a conflict, and its origin fields only under patch_branch_source origin
Make the counts agree with the patches listed, proved by a generative test, and report 0 rerere resolutions when they cannot be read
Refuse a workspace that is not carry_patch with 400

tasks.title: Queue a rebuild when a patch branch is pushed
steps: Add this task's behaviours to the rebuild trigger integration test file, and confirm they fail
At the after-push step package 07 left for it, queue a rebuild when an accepted update touched a registered patch branch and auto_rebuild_after_push is not false
Do not make the push's answer wait for the rebuild

Queue at most one rebuild per workspace whatever the trigger, so a push, a sync and a reset never produce a second while one is queued or running, and report rebuild_triggered false where the caller is told

tasks.title: Verify the patch stack end to end against a running deployment
steps: Add the four smoke tests and confirm each passes against a running deployment with a real upstream and fork and the real afc binary, or skips with a message naming what was missing

Trace 09-PATH-1: the add resolves the branch in the real repository, the submit queues a real job, the job drives the history engine of package 06 against the repository store of package 05, and the integration branch is set
Trace 09-PATH-2: the sync fetches the real upstream, the merged-upstream detection reads real commits, and the queued rebuild retires the merged patch
Trace 09-PATH-3: the conflict reaches the resolution store of package 06 and the second rebuild replays it, with no fixture standing in for either
Trace 09-PATH-4: the divergence is found against the real fork and the reset keeps the old tip where package 05's capability report says replaced tips are kept

For every criterion carrying a contract, confirm a caller in production code consumes the producer's result and not only a test: the branch resolution is called by the add, the history engine by the rebuild and the preview, the trigger by the push, the sync and the reset, and the capability report by the replaced-tip handling
Confirm the rebuild holds the workspace lock only at its start and its end by running a sync and a branch push while a rebuild applies patches
Grep src/patch/, src/rebuild/, src/sync/ and the files every task's touches lists for TODO, FIXME and the project's not-implemented marker, and remove any that remain
Add the carry-patch conformance cases to the harness from package 01
done_when: `make check` passes with no network access and no deployment configured
afc patch, afc rebuild, afc rerere and afc workspace patch-status behave as docs/prd/cli.md specifies against a running deployment
